meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы с Викой расстались, и она сразу кого-то нашла?
examples.trans: You and Vika broke up, and she immediately found someone?
Better late than never.
I promise, I never will again.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.text: Когда теряешь любовь, жизнь лишается всякого смысла.
examples.trans: When you lose love, life loses all meaning.
You're wasting your time.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'love' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We are exchanging curious facts, after all.

examples.text: Когда теряешь любовь, жизнь лишается всякого смысла.

examples.trans: For the first time I sang of love!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Relax and enjoy life.

examples.text: Тебе на это ещё всю жизнь смотреть.
examples.trans: You still have to look at this your whole life.

examples.text: От этого зависит вся моя жизнь.
examples.trans: My entire life depends on this.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is deprived of / loses'.

related.gloss: not to is deprived of (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и лишаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and is deprived of on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют лишаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to is deprived of.

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.text: Когда теряешь любовь, жизнь лишается всякого смысла.
examples.trans: When you lose love, life loses all meaning.
Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In what sense?

examples.text: Когда теряешь любовь, жизнь лишается всякого смысла.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This is not your child.

examples.text: Ну чей это ребёнок, если не твой?
examples.trans: Well whose child is it, if not yours?

examples.text: Убедиться в том, что ребёнок твой, очень просто.
examples.trans: Making sure that the child is yours is very simple.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А Костя вообще врать не умеет.
examples.trans: And Kostya does not know how to lie at all.
I need to talk with the doctor.

examples.text: Вика, мне твой врач всё рассказал.
examples.trans: Vika, your doctor told me everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Calm down, I will leave everything to a professional.

examples.text: Кате всё равно правду не расскажешь.
examples.trans: You cannot tell Katya the truth anyway.
Alright, it is settled, we are going.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Обо мне ведь ничего не рассказал.
examples.trans: After all, you told her nothing about me.

examples.text: Настя, ну я не могу тебе рассказать.
examples.trans: Nastya, well I cannot tell you.
Kostik told me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Great, so you know everything.
I know this town really well!
Everything went great.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А это значит ярко и красочно.
examples.trans: And this means brightly and colorfully.

examples.text: Витя, объясни мне, что это значит!
examples.trans: Vitya, explain to me what this means!
So she told the truth.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
In a divorce, two people are always at fault.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Я узнала о тебе много нового.
examples.trans: I learned a lot of new things about you.

examples.text: Даже не знаешь человека и защищаешь его.
examples.trans: You do not even know the man and you defend him.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: А меня Виктория просила ничего не говорить.
examples.trans: And Victoria asked me not to say anything.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'father' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он хотел в чём-то мне признаться.
examples.trans: He wanted to confess something to me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.

examples.text: Как у тебя дела, всё хорошо?
examples.trans: How are you doing, is everything fine?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The money will go to charity.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'срочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('indefinite / permanent').

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'worked out'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и сложиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and worked out on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют сложиться.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, this is very important.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'led, behaved', paired with 'повести'.

examples.text: Я обещаю вести себя крайне аккуратно.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello (on the phone)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, good evening.
Hello? Who's this?
Hello, Viktor Stepanovich?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.trans: Good morning!
Hello, good evening.
Good evening!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Go to our place, we will talk tonight.
Hello, good evening.
Good evening!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Your husband turned out to be very persistent.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You blabber about your ex-husband.

examples.text: От тебя же все мужики сбегают.
examples.trans: All men run away from you.

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turned out to be', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?

examples.text: Если ты не хочешь, я не буду тебя заставлять.
examples.trans: If you do not want to, I will not force you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стырный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('persistent').

examples.trans: Your husband turned out to be very persistent.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень настырный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very persistent choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Обо мне ведь ничего не рассказал.
examples.trans: After all, you told her nothing about me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to him', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Eleonora had an unhappy marriage.

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, ты думаешь, я ничего не понимаю?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Она просила меня забрать её анализы.

examples.text: Познакомь, а то мне придётся Катю просить.
examples.trans: Introduce us, or else I will have to ask Katya.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, Nastya!
Thank you, everything is very delicious.
Thank you for your vigilance.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('very much, big').

examples.trans: But I cannot anymore.
I promise, I never will again.
